newsitem.title: USA: High Plains reopening ethanol plants.
newsitem.headline: High Plains reopening ethanol plants.

text.p: High Plains Corp said Wednesday its Colwich, Kan. ethanol plant, which was shut down in May due to high grain prices, will reopen on September 15.

"Grain deliveries at an initial cost of $3.00 a bushel have begun, plant employees have returned to work, and we expect to manufacture fuel grade ethanol there at the full production rate of 20 million gallons per year," Stanley Larson, chief executive officer, said in a statement.
Production of fuel grade ethanol at the York, Neb. plant, which was also halted in May, is expected to resume soon.
A spokesman said timing of the resumption of production will depend on the corn harvest.

"The harvest of grain at York is slightly behind the Kansas harvest, but like the Kansas corn and milo harvest, is expected to yield record or near-record crops," Larson said. "Our York plant is expected to resume operations at its full 40 million gallon per year production rate as well."
Larson said High Plains has purchased more than three million bushels of corn at net costs of $3.00 per bushel or less and expects to buy more at even lower prices when the harvest is underway.
Earlier, High Plains announced a $17 million contract for high grade industrial grade ethanol.
High Plains said it also presold a significant portion of its production of fuel grade ethanol for the upcoming winter at price levels as high as $1.53 a gallon.

"By contracting to lock in these ethanol prices, and with corn costs projected to continue to decline, the company anticipates good profitability for the second and third fiscal quarters," Larson said.
